sentences.text: This animal possessed a long and broad snout, extremely wide nostrils, and many small tooth sockets in the upper jaw.
The only known specimen is a skull lacking the lower jaw, cataloged as AMNH 5178.
This single holotype serves as the basis for the entire genus.
The genus was named by Mook in 1926.
It is currently classified within the subfamily Caimaninae.
While later publications placed it in Crocodylidae, recent analyses suggest it might be a pristichampsid or a synonym of Pristichampsus.
A 1999 study placed Orthogenysuchus in a new clade that also included the Miocene caimanines Purussaurus and Mourasuchus.
Orthogenysuchus predates Purussaurus and Mourasuchus by approximately 30 million years, implying significant ghost lineages for those groups.
The proposed clade linking Orthogenysuchus and Mourasuchus remains informally described because it relies on ambiguous characters due to the poor preservation of the holotype.
Fossils were recovered from the Wasatch Beds of the Willwood Formation in Wyoming.
It lived during the Ypresian stage, between 56 and 51.1 million years ago.
